TrueLift

Restaurant discounts on Zomato are judged by the orders that use them. TrueLift judges them by the orders they create, inside the owner's OTP approval.

Since August 2026, every restaurant-funded offer needs the owner's OTP

  1. July–August 2026. Restaurant owners in Bengaluru object to discounts deducted without clear consent. They ask for approval for a fixed period, fresh approval to extend it, and itemised payouts.
  2. 8 August 2026. Zomato agrees: restaurant-funded campaigns are opt-in and start only after the owner approves them by OTP.
  3. Now. An owner who cannot see whether an offer pays has every reason to stop approving it.

in Q2 FY27, up 41% from ₹806 Cr a year earlier. Discounting is rising again, so knowing what it buys is worth more.

Notes, slide 2

The OTP turns every discount into a decision the owner signs. Today the owner signs blind: the report afterwards counts orders that used the offer, not orders it created.

₹60 off a ₹400 order pays only if 32 of every 100 orders using it are extra

One orderFull price₹60 off
Food sales₹400₹400
Discount–−₹60
Commission (25% of the bill)−₹100−₹85
GST on commission (18%)−₹18−₹15.30
Food and packaging (37%)−₹148−₹148
Restaurant keeps₹134₹91.70

Each order that would have come anyway now earns ₹42.30 less. Each extra order earns ₹91.70.

So the offer breaks even when 32 in 100 of its orders are extra; 45 in 100 if commission is charged on the bill before the discount.

Computed by truelift/economics.py, the code the service uses.

Notes, slide 3

One order, exact. Commission is 25% of the bill plus 18% GST on it, food and packaging 37%. The break-even is 32%: below that share of extra orders, the discount loses money.

Whether commission is charged before or after the discount is a question for Eternal; we ran both.

The report counts every order that used the offer. It cannot say which ones the offer created

Notes, slide 4

This is the core of the problem. The report shows 100 orders and every one looks like a success. In our simulated market 60 of them would have happened anyway.

TrueLift adds four calls to the offer flow Zomato already has

1

Quote

Before the OTP

A forecast of extra orders and profit with a range, and a better version of the same discount, or no offer.

2

Serve

Customer opens a menu

A table lookup decides who sees the discount; 1 in 10 eligible customers is held out.

3

Payout

Every week

The restaurant pays for its own offer, itemised. Zomato co-funds only what it measures.

4

Measure

Every week

Held-out customers against the rest: extra profit with a range, on WhatsApp. Renewal needs a new OTP.

No new screens: the forecast sits on the OTP screen, the result arrives on WhatsApp, and nothing changes in how customers order.

TrueLiftdocs/architecture.md, docs/integration_blueprint.md5
Notes, slide 5

Four hooks. The quote is the only one the owner sees before signing; serving is a lookup, no model on the customer's path; the held-out customers are what make the weekly number true.

Try it: you own a restaurant. Create an offer

  1. Tap Create an offer. Your usual ₹60 off is already set.
  2. Read the forecast, then tap Use this version.
  3. Continue to approve and enter the OTP shown on screen.
  4. Tap Simulate the first week, then each next week.
  5. Tap Send to my WhatsApp: the owner's weekly message.

Every answer on the public demo was computed by the service and saved, so nothing you tap can break it. The guided demo tells the same story in ten steps.

The simulator knows the truth, so every estimate is checked against it

Weekly result: truth inside the 80% range

  • "Keep" verdicts truly positive: 140 of 142 after one week, 111 of 111 after four.
  • Placebo offers that change nothing: paused 1.8% over four weekly looks (the old rule: 18.4%).
  • Real randomised data (ads and e-mail, not food): uplift models beat the shortcut in all five splits of Hillstrom's women's e-mail; on Criteo's purchases the shortcut wins (92% against 72%). We report both.
TrueLiftSources: reports/evaluation.json, reports/uplift_validation_*.json. Customers, orders and profits are simulated on 300 real 2019 Bengaluru listings.9
Notes, slide 9

Ranges are built to miss about one time in five: after one week they do, and later they miss less often. A pause needs the offer's own control group to show a loss, so placebo offers are almost never paused.

Say the real-data result honestly: on one dataset the simple shortcut wins.

Leader: When TrueLift says keep, it is right 111 times in 111 after four weeks.

Domain expert: The owner sees a range that narrows every week as the restaurant's own evidence grows.

Engineer: Combined estimate: the offer's control group plus the model, weighted by noise that is re-estimated every week across running offers; the pause uses an always-valid boundary.

We audited our own work: 50 findings, all fixed. Two limits remain

Three of the fixes

  • Serving and measurement held out different customers. Now one hashed assignment, used and tested everywhere.
  • The simulator paid Zomato's co-funding on every redemption. Now only for customers new to Zomato, exactly as the engine does.
  • Placebo offers were paused on noise. A pause now needs the offer's own always-valid evidence.

What is still not right

  • A suggested version's stated advantage is about five times its true one, though 79% truly beat the owner's.
  • The four-week estimate over-states the truth by ₹452 an offer on average, inherited from the model.

From prototype to pilot: measure first, change who sees offers later

1

Shadow holdout

2% of eligible customers held out of offers owners already run, in one city. Nothing shown to owners.

2

Measure

Forecast and weekly result for a random half of the pilot restaurants: 356 in each half, 712 in all.

3

Target

Owners in that half may let TrueLift choose who sees the offer.

4

Scale

City by city, with the same guardrails.

Each phase starts only when the one before has passed its checks (sample-ratio checks, placebo offers, renewal rate) and stops at once if a guardrail is breached. The shadow kit already measures offers from logs in Zomato's event format.

TrueLiftdocs/integration_blueprint.md, reports/pilot_sample_size.json11
Notes, slide 11

The pilot is sized to detect a rise in renewals from 60% to 70% with 80% power; the 60% is a placeholder Eternal would replace with its own figure.

What we would like from Eternal

  1. Is commission charged on the bill before or after the discount? (Break-even 32% against 45% at ₹60 off a ₹400 order.)
  2. Could we run the shadow kit on anonymised offer logs for one city?
  3. What does the OTP approval screen show today, and how often do owners decline?

Appendix: how the pieces fit

Partner app

Owner creates an offer → quote → OTP → consent record (hash-chained, stores the forecast shown)

Customer app

Menu opens → serve: decision-table lookup and the (customer, offer) hash → exposure log

Every week

Exposure log + orders → measure → WhatsApp result, payout lines, renewal on evidence

Learning

Every held-out and shown visit is randomised training data; a candidate model is promoted only if it ranks recent held-out weeks better

The offer's own control group alone is unbiased but noisy; the model alone is steady but can be wrong; TrueLift combines them by how noisy each is, re-estimated every week across running offers. Where a claim stops holding (sensitivity sweep)

  • TrueLift earns Zomato more commission than blanket offers: no longer holds when price sensitivity of every customer type is 1.3
  • TrueLift earns Zomato more commission than blanket offers: no longer holds when food cost, share of the menu price is 0.45
  • TrueLift earns restaurants more from their own offers than the simple rule: no longer holds when share of customers who are deal-seekers is 0.35
  • TrueLift earns Zomato more commission than blanket offers: no longer holds when share of customers who are deal-seekers is 0.35
  • TrueLift earns restaurants more from their own offers than the simple rule: no longer holds when truelift's holdout share is 0.2
TrueLiftSources: reports/evaluation.json (seeds), reports/sensitivity.json. Customers, orders and profits are simulated on 300 real 2019 Bengaluru listings.A4

Say the boundaries plainly; they are the honest answer to 'what if your assumptions are wrong'.

Appendix: research with restaurant owners

One interview so far. On 17 November a team member showed the demo to the manager of a chain outlet in Gandhinagar; its note is not written up yet.

The kit for the rest is ready: question sheets in English (Hindi and Gujarati drafts), a consent script, comprehension cards that put today's offer report beside TrueLift's weekly result, and a note template.

What we will bring back: whether commission is charged before or after the discount, what an offer report and the OTP screen show, and which wording owners read correctly.

Appendix: what it costs to run

  • The control group. Holding out 1 in 10 eligible customers gives up ₹87,664 of restaurant profit a week across the 300 restaurants (719 orders). It is the price of knowing.
  • Serving. A lookup and a hash per menu open; decision tables are built when an offer is approved.
  • Quotes and measurement. Batch work: a quote when an owner creates an offer, a measurement once a week per offer.
  • Model. Two gradient-boosted classifiers retrained on new randomised data, promoted only if better on recent held-out weeks.
TrueLiftSource: reports/evaluation.json (zomato_ledger). Customers, orders and profits are simulated on 300 real 2019 Bengaluru listings.A8
